A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching algorithms, experiments and substantial shared proofs. All 30 pages of v1 and 54 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: Section 8 and Figure 1 report original Gaussian-bandit simulations comparing REC, RSE, RASMAB and UCB1, averaged over 300 runs.

after.justification: Section 8 reports original simulations through updated Figure 1 and new Table 2, including terminal regrets and uncertainty bounds.

M1.justification: REC, RSE and RLSE retain their algorithm steps, sampling schedules, randomized confidence thresholds, elimination mechanisms and G-optimal exploration. The new randomization theorem analyzes existing components rather than changing the procedures.

E1.justification: Coverage remains a ten-arm Gaussian problem with equal suboptimality gaps and a three-arm Gaussian problem with unequal gaps. v1's reference to 'three models' is corrected to 'two'; neither version actually reports a third scenario. Model 1's parameter revision is assessed under E3.

E2.justification: RASMAB, identified as Algorithm 2 of Esfandiari et al. (2023), and UCB1 remain the external comparators in both models. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 8 changes Model 1's stated means from one 0.9 and nine 0.1 values to one 0.7 and nine 0.3 values. Model 2's means, variance 0.5, horizon 10,000 and grid-search target of empirical nonreplication 0.3 remain unchanged. This establishes a reported setting revision without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: No new ablation, sensitivity study, robustness test or empirical case study is reported. The two simulation scenarios remain; the added appendix theorem is theoretical, and expanded explanations of algorithm behavior belong to C2.

E5.justification: Both versions report 300-run averages and the same empirical nonreplication estimator. v2 newly provides two-sigma confidence bounds using plug-in variance in Table 2. This adds uncertainty reporting without documenting an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Figure 1's curves change in both models, and Table 2 newly supplies eight terminal-regret entries. Under the retained stated Model 2 setting, REC's endpoint changes from approximately 1,620 in v1's figure to 1,821.0 in v2's table. Model 1's revised means prevent interpreting its changed scores as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2's Theorem 12 replaces v1's Theorem 5 by removing the uniformly-good assumption and truncating the lower bound with TΔ; Appendix G adds the corresponding finite-horizon case analysis. New Appendix B also proves Theorem 17: deterministic no-regret algorithms cannot be replicable for any ρ < 1/2. These substantially extend the formal content.

C1.justification: The central claim that replicability has negligible asymptotic regret cost remains. v2 adds an explicit limiting regret-ratio claim of at most ρ²/K² and narrows the introductory linear-bandit contribution from regret 'independent of K' to regret scaling linearly with d.

C2.justification: v1 qualitatively connects replicability with reduced estimation bias; v2 adds a concrete z-test error-control argument. v2 also interprets tuned RASMAB as RSE with ρa = 0 and explains why merely shuffling exploration allocations, as discussed for Perchet et al., does not supply the required randomization.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 states that simulations took less than one hour on a JupyterHub server using a standard desktop machine. v1 provides no corresponding runtime or environment information. The disclosure remains brief and supplies no code-access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on reproducibility, healthcare and privacy, including Baker, Pineau et al., Collins et al. and Narayanan and Shmatikov. It acknowledges Zhang et al. (2024)'s stateful bandit setting while qualifying Esfandiari et al.'s exclusivity. The Hyperband and Gat–Goldwasser references disappear; the main positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the abstract, introductory motivation, crowdsourcing example and conclusion, alongside terminology and affiliation edits. Notation and randomization appendices are added before the retained appendices. The main section sequence and most algorithm and proof prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset with different typography, substantially wider line spacing, revised title formatting and removal of running headers. Algorithms gain line numbers, Figure 1 is resized and relocated, and numerical-results Table 2 and notation Table 3 are added. These are document-wide display changes beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: The broader lower bound, randomization-necessity proof and confidence intervals improve theoretical scope and assessability. However, Section 1.1 adds a claimed 5% testing guarantee whose displayed z-statistic omits variance and unequal-allocation normalization, without establishing the necessary assumptions. These substantive gains coexist with a new unsupported practical-inference claim, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
